A 34-year-old teacher develops an <b>abrupt onset of high fever</b>, chills, <b>myalgia</b>, <b>headache</b>, and <b>generalized weakness</b>, followed by sore throat and dry cough, about <b>2 days</b> after several colleagues fell ill. Six days later she has a new productive cough with lobar consolidation (<b>secondary bacterial pneumonia</b>). The virus escapes immunity by <b>antigenic drift and shift</b>, and she is treated with a <b>neuraminidase inhibitor</b>.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b>Influenza virus (A, B)</b><div><small>Orthomyxoviridae · segmented (−)ssRNA</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Influenza</b> (ไข้หวัดใหญ่)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td><b>Abrupt onset</b> of fever, <b>myalgia</b>, headache, generalized weakness + URTI symptoms</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td><b>Respiratory droplets</b> · Influenza A ติดได้ทั้ง <b>birds & mammals</b>; B, C: primarily humans</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td>Worldwide · seasonal epidemics; antigenic shift (Influenza A) → pandemics</td></tr></table><ul><li>Subtype ตาม <b>hemagglutinin (HA)</b> และ <b>neuraminidase (NA)</b>; Influenza B มี 2 clades: Yamagata, Victoria</li><li><b>Antigenic drift</b> = accumulation of point mutations · <b>Antigenic shift</b> = <b>reassortment</b> of genome segments (Influenza A ติดได้ทั้ง birds และ mammals)</li><li>Complications: secondary infection จาก <i>S. aureus</i>, <i>S. pneumoniae</i>; <b>pericarditis, myocarditis, myositis, rhabdomyolysis</b>, Reye syndrome, transverse myelitis, aseptic meningitis</li><li>Antivirals: <b>oseltamivir</b>, peramivir, zanamivir (NA inhibitors) · <b>baloxavir</b> (cap-dependent endonuclease inhibitor)</li><li><b>Rapid antigen detection tests (RADTs)</b> lack sensitivity เทียบกับ molecular assays</li></ul><small>Viral diseases 69 · หน้า 2–3</small>	PathogenDx::Viral::resp
A 2-year-old boy has had rhinorrhea and low-grade fever for 2 days. Tonight he developed a <b>barking, seal-like cough</b>, a hoarse voice, and <b>inspiratory stridor</b> that worsens when he cries; he is not drooling. A frontal neck radiograph shows <b>subglottic narrowing (steeple sign)</b>. The responsible virus causes <b>nearly half of all cases of laryngotracheitis (croup)</b>.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b>Parainfluenza virus (PIV-1)</b><div><small>Paramyxoviridae · 4 species</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Croup</b> (laryngotracheitis) · bronchiolitis & pneumonia (PIV-3)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>URTI prodrome → <b>barking cough</b>, hoarseness, <b>inspiratory stridor</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td>Inspiratory stridor; <b>steeple sign</b> (subglottic narrowing) on AP neck X-ray</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td>Respiratory droplets, direct contact</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td>Young children; severe LRTI in young children & elderly</td></tr></table><ul><li>Croup ส่วนใหญ่เกิดจาก <b>PIV-1</b> · <b>bronchiolitis & pneumonia</b> ส่วนใหญ่เกิดจาก <b>PIV-3</b></li><li>4 species; incubation 2–6 วัน; ~15% เป็น <b>LRTI</b> (มักในเด็ก)</li><li><b>Severe LRTI</b> ใน young children และ elderly</li><li>No targeted therapeutics → <b>supportive</b></li></ul><small>Viral diseases 69 · หน้า 4</small>	PathogenDx::Viral::resp
A 3-month-old boy born at <b>32 weeks’ gestation</b> develops rhinorrhea and cough, followed by <b>tachypnea</b>, nasal flaring, chest retractions, and diffuse <b>wheezing</b> (<b>bronchiolitis</b>). He caught it through <b>large droplets</b> from his sibling’s nasal secretions. Lung tissue from a fatal case of the same infection shows <b>multinucleated syncytial giant cells</b> with <b>round pink intracytoplasmic inclusions</b>. High-risk infants can receive <b>palivizumab</b> prophylaxis.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b>Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)</b><div><small>Pneumoviridae · (−)ssRNA</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Bronchiolitis</b> / pneumonia in infants</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>Rhinorrhea, cough → <b>tachypnea, wheezing</b>; most severe in premature infants</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td>Wheezing, chest retractions, nasal flaring · histo: <b>syncytial giant cells</b> + intracytoplasmic inclusion</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td><b>Large droplets</b> from nasopharyngeal secretions</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td><b>Infants</b> (esp. premature), elderly, immunocompromised</td></tr></table><ul><li>รุนแรงที่สุดใน <b>premature newborns</b> (narrow terminal airways); elderly & immunocompromised ก็รุนแรงได้; reinfection พบบ่อยแต่เบากว่า</li><li>vs Adenovirus: RSV = <b>syncytia + intracytoplasmic inclusion</b> · Adenovirus = <b>smudge cell (intranuclear inclusion)</b> (MED28 ข้อ 1 เฉลย Adenovirus)</li><li>Tx: supportive + O<sub>2</sub>; <b>ribavirin</b> (aerosol/IV)</li></ul><small>Viral diseases 69 · หน้า 4–5</small>	PathogenDx::Viral::resp
A 4-year-old girl is admitted with fever, cough, wheezing, and hypoxemia from <b>severe lower respiratory tract infection</b>, while her parents had only <b>mild self-limited cold symptoms</b>. A multiplex respiratory NAAT is negative for RSV and influenza but positive for a <b>pneumovirus closely related to RSV</b> that infects <b>all age groups</b> and is found in about <b>13% of severe pediatric LRTIs requiring hospitalization</b>. No targeted antiviral is available.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b>Human metapneumovirus (hMPV)</b><div><small>Pneumoviridae (closely related to RSV)</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td>URTI → severe LRTI in children</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>Mostly <b>asymptomatic / self-limited URTI</b>; bronchiolitis, pneumonia in children</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td>Respiratory droplets</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td>All age groups · 13% of severe pediatric LRTIs requiring hospitalization (US)</td></tr></table><ul><li>Healthy children & adults: commonly asymptomatic หรือ self-limited URTI</li><li>Tx: <b>supportive</b></li></ul><small>Viral diseases 69 · หน้า 5</small>	PathogenDx::Viral::resp
A 25-year-old office worker has sneezing, sore throat, and <b>profuse watery nasal discharge</b> beginning <b>2–3 days</b> after his daughter had a cold; he is afebrile. A week later he develops ear pain from <b>acute otitis media</b> and facial pressure from <b>sinusitis</b>. The responsible virus is the <b>most common cause of the common cold</b> worldwide, and one species (type C) causes severe lower respiratory infection in children with <b>asthma</b>.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b>Rhinovirus</b><div><small>Picornaviridae</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Common cold</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td><b>Pronounced watery nasal discharge</b> (incubation 2–3 days); complications: acute otitis media, sinusitis</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td>Respiratory droplets, hand contact (fomites)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td>Worldwide — most common respiratory virus; Rhinovirus C → severe LRTI in young children, elderly, asthma</td></tr></table><ul><li><b>Most common cause</b> ของ respiratory viral infections ทั่วโลก</li><li><b>Rhinovirus C</b> → <b>severe LRTI</b> ใน young children, elderly, immunocompromised และ underlying lung disease เช่น <b>asthma</b></li></ul><small>Viral diseases 69 · หน้า 6</small>	PathogenDx::Viral::resp
Twenty students at a <b>boarding school</b> become ill within a week of using the same <b>swimming pool</b>. A 14-year-old presents with low-grade fever, <b>pharyngitis</b>, rhinitis, and red watery eyes. Examination shows <b>bilateral follicular conjunctivitis</b> and tender <b>preauricular lymphadenopathy</b>. The non-enveloped dsDNA virus spreads by aerosolized droplets or <b>direct conjunctival inoculation</b> and also causes outbreaks among <b>military recruits</b>.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b>Adenovirus</b><div><small>Adenoviridae · dsDNA, non-enveloped</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Pharyngoconjunctival fever</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>Low-grade fever + <b>pharyngitis</b> + <b>conjunctivitis</b> + rhinitis</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td><b>Bilateral follicular conjunctivitis</b> + <b>preauricular lymphadenopathy</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td><b>Aerosolized droplets</b> or <b>direct conjunctival inoculation</b> (pool water)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td><b>Crowded populations</b>: boarding school, summer camp, <b>swimming pool</b>, military recruits</td></tr></table><ul><li><b>Keratoconjunctivitis (pink eye)</b> with or without URTI symptoms</li><li>Important cause of <b>childhood diarrhea</b> (<b>species F, types 40 & 41</b>)</li><li>Vulnerable patients → <b>severe pneumonia</b></li></ul><small>Viral diseases 69 · หน้า 6 · ★ โจทย์เก่า MED29 ข้อ 10</small>	PathogenDx::Viral::resp MED29-10
A 2-year-old boy has had low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, <b>tachypnea</b>, and <b>wheezing</b> for 5 days and dies of respiratory failure despite intensive care. Autopsy lung shows <b>necrotizing bronchiolitis</b>; the bronchiolar epithelial cells contain <b>large basophilic intranuclear inclusions</b> that obscure the nuclear border (<b>smudge cells</b>). No syncytial giant cells or intracytoplasmic inclusions are seen.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b>Adenovirus</b><div><small>Adenoviridae · dsDNA, non-enveloped</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Necrotizing bronchiolitis</b> / pneumonia</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>Low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, <b>tachypnea, wheezing</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td>Histo: <b>smudge cells</b> (basophilic intranuclear inclusion)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td>Aerosolized droplets</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td>Young children; severe pneumonia in vulnerable / immunocompromised patients</td></tr></table><ul><li><b>Smudge cell</b> = <b>basophilic intranuclear inclusion</b> ± multinucleated giant cells</li><li>vs <b>RSV</b>: syncytial cells + <b>intracytoplasmic</b> inclusions</li><li>vs <b>CMV</b>: <b>cytomegaly</b> + <b>owl’s eye intranuclear inclusion</b> + perinuclear halo</li></ul><small>Viral diseases 69 · หน้า 6 · โจทย์เก่า · ★ โจทย์เก่า MED28 ข้อ 1</small>	PathogenDx::Viral::resp MED28-1
A 58-year-old man with diabetes and obesity (BMI 32) develops fever, cough, myalgia, headache, and a <b>sudden loss of smell and taste (anosmia, ageusia)</b> 5 days after a family gathering. On day 8 he becomes short of breath with <b>hypoxemia</b> and bilateral ground-glass opacities, progressing to <b>ARDS</b> and a <b>pulmonary embolism</b>. Labs show <b>lymphopenia</b> and a raised CRP. Electron microscopy of the virus shows <b>crown-like surface spikes</b>.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b>SARS-CoV-2</b><div><small>Coronaviridae · crown-like spikes on EM</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>COVID-19</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>Headache, myalgia, <b>cough</b>, sore throat, diarrhea, <b>anosmia / ageusia</b>; severe: pneumonia, hypoxia, ARDS</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td>Hypoxia + abnormal CXR; children: <b>MIS-C</b> (Kawasaki-like)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td><b>Droplets</b>, direct contact, <b>aerosol</b>; possible fecal-oral and animal-to-human</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td>Worldwide; severe in elderly, DM, CKD, cardiovascular disease, COPD, obesity</td></tr></table><ul><li>Incubation เฉลี่ย <b>5–6 days</b> (>97% มีอาการภายใน 14 วัน); ~40% asymptomatic; severe (pneumonia, hypoxia) 15–20%</li><li><b>R0</b>: original strain 2.5 · Delta ~7 · Omicron ~10</li><li>Risk of severe disease: elderly, DM, CKD, cardiovascular disease, COPD, obesity (BMI ≥30)</li><li>Human coronaviruses 7 strains — 4 strains ทำให้ common cold (NL63, 229E, OC43, HKU1)</li></ul><small>Viral diseases 69 · หน้า 50–52</small>	PathogenDx::Viral::resp
An <b>unimmunized</b> 5-year-old girl has high fever with <b>cough, coryza, and conjunctivitis</b> for 3 days. Examination shows <b>white punctate papules on the buccal mucosa opposite the lower molars</b> (<b>Koplik spots</b>). The next day a <b>maculopapular rash</b> appears <b>behind the ears and on the face</b>, then <b>spreads downward</b> to the trunk and limbs and becomes confluent. A lymph node biopsy would show <b>Warthin-Finkeldey giant cells</b>; she is given <b>vitamin A</b>.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b>Measles virus (Measles morbillivirus)</b><div><small>Paramyxoviridae (Morbillivirus) · enveloped (−)ssRNA</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Measles</b> (หัด, rubeola)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>High fever + <b>3Cs</b> (cough, coryza, conjunctivitis) → maculopapular rash</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td><b>Koplik spots</b> (buccal mucosa opposite lower molars) · rash starts <b>face / behind the ears → spreads downward</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td><b>Respiratory droplets & aerosol</b> (highly contagious)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td>Unimmunized children; severe in <b>vitamin A deficiency</b>, malnutrition, immunocompromised</td></tr></table><ul><li>Highly contagious: ~<b>90%</b> of susceptible contacts infected; respiratory droplets & aerosol; <b>incubation 11–13 days</b></li><li>Histo: <b>Warthin-Finkeldey giant cells</b> (eosinophilic intranuclear + intracytoplasmic inclusions) ใน lymph node / sputum</li><li>Complications: <b>giant cell pneumonia</b>, diarrhea, encephalitis (APME, MIBE, <b>SSPE</b> — ได้ถึง 15 ปีหลังติด), <b>keratitis / blindness</b> (vitamin A deficiency)</li><li>Dx: <b>serum IgM</b> (sens 91% วันที่ 0–3 หลัง rash → 100% เมื่อ >7 วัน), <b>RT-PCR</b> (throat/NP swab, urine, serum)</li><li>Tx: supportive + <b>vitamin A supplementation</b> + treat secondary bacterial infection</li></ul><small>Viral diseases 69 · หน้า 8–10 · ★ โจทย์เก่า MED23 ข้อ 10</small>	PathogenDx::Viral::kids MED23-10
A 24-year-old woman at <b>10 weeks of pregnancy</b> has mild fever and tender <b>postauricular lymphadenopathy</b>, followed by a <b>fine, pink, non-coalescing maculopapular rash</b> that starts on the face, spreads to the trunk within <b>24 hours</b>, and fades after <b>3 days</b>. Small red spots are seen on the <b>soft palate</b> (<b>Forchheimer spots</b>). Her baby is born small for gestational age with <b>cataracts</b>, <b>sensorineural hearing loss</b>, and a <b>cardiac defect</b>.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b>Rubella virus</b><div><small>Matonaviridae (เดิม Togaviridae) · enveloped (+)ssRNA</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Rubella</b> (หัดเยอรมัน, German measles, three-day measles) · <b>congenital rubella syndrome</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>Mild fever + <b>fine pink non-coalescing rash</b> (face → trunk ใน 24 ชม., หายใน 3 days)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td><b>Forchheimer spots</b> (soft palate), postauricular lymphadenopathy · CRS: <b>cataracts, SNHL, cardiac defects</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td>Direct / <b>droplet contact</b> with nasopharyngeal secretions · <b>transplacental</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td>Non-immune pregnant women — first trimester (~85% defects) · TORCH</td></tr></table><ul><li>Maternal infection มัก <b>mild & nonspecific</b>; birth defects สูงสุดเมื่อติดใน <b>first trimester (~85%)</b></li><li><b>Congenital rubella syndrome (CRS)</b>: <b>SGA</b> + <b>cataracts, SNHL, cardiac defects</b></li><li>No effective antiviral; CRS → supportive care</li></ul><small>Viral diseases 69 · หน้า 10–11</small>	PathogenDx::Viral::kids
A 10-month-old boy has had a <b>high fever (39.8 °C) for 4 days</b> but looks well apart from one febrile seizure. When the <b>fever suddenly resolves</b>, a <b>nonpruritic, blanching macular rash</b> appears <b>on the trunk</b> and then spreads to the neck, face, and extremities. In transplant recipients, reactivation of the same latent virus causes posttransplant fever, encephalitis, and pneumonitis.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b>Human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6; HHV-7 พบน้อยกว่า)</b><div><small>Herpesviridae (beta) · dsDNA</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Roseola infantum</b> (exanthem subitum, sixth disease)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td><b>High fever 3–5 days</b> → <b>rash appears as fever subsides</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td><b>Nonpruritic blanching macular rash</b> starting on the <b>trunk</b> → neck, face, extremities</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td>Saliva (oral secretions)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td>Infants 6 months–2 years · reactivation in transplant recipients</td></tr></table><ul><li>Rash เริ่มที่ <b>trunk</b> แล้วลามออก (ต่างจาก measles ที่เริ่มที่ face แล้วลามลง)</li><li><b>Reactivation</b> ใน <b>transplant recipients</b> → posttransplantation fever, encephalitis, pneumonitis</li><li>Dx: <b>qPCR</b> ใน blood / CSF (quantitation ช่วยบอก clinical significance และ monitor treatment)</li></ul><small>Viral diseases 69 · หน้า 11–12</small>	PathogenDx::Viral::kids
A 7-year-old girl has a few days of low-grade fever and malaise, followed by a bright red, confluent rash on both cheeks (<b>“slapped-cheek” appearance</b>) and, days later, a <b>lacy reticular rash</b> on the trunk and limbs. Her mother develops <b>symmetric arthralgia</b> of the small joints of the hands. A 60-year-old man with <b>hereditary spherocytosis</b> has 1 week of progressive fatigue, pallor, and exertional dyspnea. A 3-year-old girl at a <b>daycare center</b> where several children are sick has fever, poor feeding, and painful <b>oral vesicles and ulcers</b> on the tongue and buccal mucosa. Examination shows <b>vesicles on the palms and soles</b> and papules on the <b>buttocks</b>. A 4-year-old boy had fever with <b>vesicles surrounded by erythematous halos on the buccal mucosa, palms, and soles</b>. The virus also spreads <b>sexually</b> and by <b>IV drug use</b>.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b>Hepatitis B virus (HBV)</b><div><small>Hepadnaviridae · DNA, oncogenic</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Hepatitis B</b> → chronic infection, cirrhosis, <b>HCC</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>Acute: jaundice, RUQ pain (incubation ~90 days); chronic: often asymptomatic</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td>Chronicity by age: <b>neonate ~90%</b> vs adult ~5%</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td><b>Vertical</b> (mother-to-child), horizontal (childhood), <b>sexual</b>, <b>IVDU</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td>Endemic in Asia & Africa · HBV-exposed infants → HBIG + vaccine at birth</td></tr></table><ul><li>Childhood infection → chronic ได้ถึง <b>95%</b> · adulthood <b>3–5%</b></li><li>HBV-exposed infant: <b>HBIG within 12 hours of birth</b></li><li>Chronic HBV Tx: <b>tenofovir</b>, <b>entecavir</b>, telbivudine; acute → supportive</li><li><b>HBV genotype</b>: prognosis & therapeutic management</li></ul><small>Viral diseases 69 · หน้า 43–46 · ★ โจทย์เก่า MED29 ข้อ 7</small>	PathogenDx::Viral::liver MED29-7
A 24-year-old asymptomatic woman acquired chronic hepatitis B <b>perinatally</b>. Gram stain shows <b>Gram-positive lancet-shaped diplococci</b>; colonies are α-hemolytic, <b>optochin-sensitive</b>, and <b>bile-soluble</b>.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b><i>Streptococcus pneumoniae</i></b><div><small>Gram+ <b>lancet-shaped diplococci</b> · α-hemolytic · optochin-sensitive · capsule</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Bacterial meningitis</b> (post-traumatic CSF leak)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td><b>High fever</b>, headache, <b>altered consciousness</b>, neck stiffness</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td><b>Nuchal rigidity</b>, Brudzinski sign; CSF: neutrophils, ↑protein, ↓glucose</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td>Normal flora of the <b>upper respiratory tract</b> → CSF leak (basilar skull fracture), otitis, pneumonia</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td><b>Adults >20 years</b> — most common community-acquired meningitis (~50%)</td></tr></table><ul><li><b>α-hemolysis</b>, <b>optochin sensitive</b>, <b>bile solubility positive</b>, capsule → <b>Quellung reaction</b></li><li>Normal inhabitant ของ <b>upper respiratory tract</b>: <b>CAP</b>, meningitis in adults, sinusitis, otitis media</li><li>Community-acquired bacterial meningitis: <i>S. pneumoniae</i> <b>~50%</b> (adults >20 y)</li></ul><small>Bacterial disease 69 · หน้า 6, 29–30 · ★ โจทย์เก่า MED25 ข้อ 5</small>	PathogenDx::Bacteria::gpc MED25-5
A 25-year-old man who had a <b>splenectomy after a car accident</b> 2 years ago presents with high fever, rigors, and <b>purulent rust-colored sputum</b>; within hours he develops septic shock and DIC. Chest radiograph shows <b>lobar consolidation</b>. Blood cultures grow <b>encapsulated Gram-positive diplococci</b> whose capsule swells with type-specific antiserum (<b>Quellung reaction</b>). A 45-year-old woman with known <b>mitral valve prolapse</b> had a <b>dental extraction without antibiotic prophylaxis</b>. Four weeks later she has <b>low-grade fever</b>, <b>night sweats</b>, fatigue, a <b>new holosystolic murmur</b>, and <b>splinter hemorrhages</b>. A 55-year-old <b>pig farmer</b> from <b>northern Thailand</b> presents with high fever, severe headache, neck stiffness, and confusion 2 days after eating <b>raw pork larb and a raw pig blood dish</b> at a village festival; he also has septic arthritis of the knee. A 9-year-old girl has a <b>sudden sore throat</b>, painful swallowing, and fever of 39 °C without cough. A 6-year-old boy has <b>acute fever and sore throat</b> with exudative tonsillitis. A 25-year-old man has an open leg fracture from a <b>farm accident</b>, with the wound <b>contaminated by soil and manure</b>. Within 24–48 hours he develops <b>severe pain</b>, swelling, bronze skin discoloration, <b>crepitus</b> in the subcutaneous tissue and muscle, a <b>foul-smelling discharge</b>, fever, and shock (<b>myonecrosis with gas formation</b>). Tissue Gram stain shows <b>large, boxcar-shaped Gram-positive rods</b>; the main virulence factor is a <b>lecithinase (α-toxin)</b>.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b><i>Clostridium perfringens</i></b><div><small>Large anaerobic Gram+ rods · spore-former · α-toxin (lecithinase)</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Gas gangrene</b> (clostridial myonecrosis) · food poisoning · necrotizing enteritis</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>Severe wound pain, rapidly spreading swelling, fever, shock within 1–3 days</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td><b>Crepitus</b> (gas in tissue), <b>foul-smelling</b> discharge, skin discoloration</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td><b>Traumatized wound</b> contaminated with <b>soil / feces</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td>Soil, GI tract; trauma, crush injuries, war wounds</td></tr></table><ul><li>มัก present ร่วมกับ Gram− rods และ various cocci</li><li><b>Food poisoning</b></li><li><b>Clostridial necrotizing enteritis</b>: enterotoxin (type C) → <b>necrosis & hemorrhage of small intestine</b>, bloody diarrhea, death ใน 24 ชม.</li></ul><small>Bacterial disease 69 · หน้า 16, 21</small>	PathogenDx::Bacteria::gpr
A 45-year-old unvaccinated gardener stepped on a <b>rusty nail</b> 10 days ago, causing a <b>deep puncture wound</b>. He now has <b>trismus (lockjaw)</b>, a fixed grimace (<b>risus sardonicus</b>), painful generalized spasms with <b>opisthotonus</b>, and hyperreflexia, plus <b>autonomic instability</b> with fluctuating blood pressure, alternating bradycardia and tachycardia, and sweating. The toxin blocks release of <b>GABA and glycine</b> from inhibitory interneurons.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b><i>Clostridium tetani</i></b><div><small>Anaerobic Gram+ rod · terminal spore (drumstick) · tetanospasmin</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Tetanus</b> (บาดทะยัก) — spastic paralysis</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td><b>Trismus (lockjaw)</b>, painful muscle spasms, <b>opisthotonus</b>, convulsion</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td><b>Risus sardonicus</b>, hyperreflexia, <b>dysautonomia</b> (labile BP, brady/tachycardia)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td><b>Puncture wound</b> (rusty nail, gardening) contaminated with soil spores</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td><b>Soil</b> (widespread); unimmunized persons; neonates — unclean umbilical cord care</td></tr></table><ul><li><b>Tetanospasmin</b> travel ตาม peripheral nerve ไป <b>anterior horn cells</b> → inhibit release of <b>GABA & glycine</b> จาก inhibitory neurons</li><li><b>Dysautonomia</b> = characteristic (ไม่ใช่ flaccid paralysis)</li><li>Neonate: <b>neonatal tetanus</b> (body rigidity)</li><li>Tx: <b>human tetanus immunoglobulin (TIG)</b>, tetanus antitoxin (<b>TAT — skin test before use</b>)</li></ul><small>Bacterial disease 69 · หน้า 17–18 · ★ โจทย์เก่า MED29 ข้อ 5</small>	PathogenDx::Bacteria::gpr MED29-5
Ten villagers in <b>northern Thailand</b> develop blurred vision, <b>diplopia</b>, <b>ptosis</b>, dysphagia, and dysarthria 12–36 hours after eating <b>home-canned bamboo shoots</b>, followed by <b>symmetric descending flaccid paralysis</b> and respiratory failure. They are <b>afebrile and alert</b>, with dilated pupils. A <b>preformed toxin</b> from an anaerobic, spore-forming Gram-positive rod blocks <b>acetylcholine release</b> at the neuromuscular junction; infants can develop a <b>“floppy baby”</b> illness after eating honey.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b><i>Clostridium botulinum</i></b><div><small>Anaerobic Gram+ rod · spore-former · botulinum toxin (blocks ACh release)</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Botulism</b> — descending flaccid paralysis</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>Diplopia, dysphagia, dysarthria → <b>descending flaccid paralysis</b> → respiratory failure; afebrile</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td><b>Ptosis</b>, dilated pupils, bulbar palsy; infant: “<b>floppy baby</b>”</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td><b>Preformed toxin</b> in improperly canned food · infant: spores (honey) · wound</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td><b>Home-canned food</b> — หน่อไม้ปี๊บ (outbreak ภาคเหนือ)</td></tr></table><ul><li><b>Most potent toxin</b> known; <b>blocks synaptic release of acetylcholine</b> (light chain cleaves <b>SNARE proteins</b>)</li><li>Food botulism = ingesting <b>preformed toxin</b></li><li><b>Infant botulism</b> = organisms produce toxin ใน infant’s gut · <b>wound botulism</b></li></ul><small>Bacterial disease 69 · หน้า 19</small>	PathogenDx::Bacteria::gpr
A 70-year-old woman receiving <b>piperacillin–tazobactam</b> for pneumonia, after an earlier course of <b>clindamycin</b>, develops profuse <b>watery diarrhea</b>, crampy lower abdominal pain, fever, and marked <b>leukocytosis</b> on day 10. Sigmoidoscopy shows <b>raised yellow-white plaques</b> on the colonic mucosa (<b>pseudomembranes</b>). Stool tests detect <b>glutamate dehydrogenase (GDH)</b> and <b>toxins A and B</b>. The spore-forming anaerobe spreads <b>fecal-orally</b> in hospitals; she is treated with oral <b>vancomycin</b>.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b><i>Clostridioides difficile</i></b><div><small>Anaerobic Gram+ rod · spore-former · toxin A (enterotoxin) + toxin B (cytotoxin)</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Pseudomembranous colitis</b> (antibiotic-associated diarrhea)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td><b>Watery diarrhea</b>, crampy abdominal pain, fever, <b>leukocytosis</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td>Endoscopy: <b>raised yellow-white plaques (pseudomembranes)</b>; toxic megacolon</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td>After <b>clindamycin / broad-spectrum antibiotics</b>; spores spread <b>fecal-oral</b> in hospitals</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td><b>Hospitalized</b> / nursing-home patients, elderly · colon</td></tr></table><ul><li>Antibiotics alter <b>normal gut flora</b> → overgrowth + <b>Toxin A (enterotoxin)</b> & <b>Toxin B (cytotoxin)</b></li><li>Dx: <b>toxin detection in feces</b>, PCR, culture — step 1 <b>GDH + toxin A/B EIA</b> → discordant → <b>NAAT / toxigenic culture</b></li><li>Tx: <b>oral vancomycin</b> หรือ metronidazole; spread by <b>fecal-oral</b> route</li></ul><small>Bacterial disease 69 · หน้า 20–21 · ★ โจทย์เก่า MED23 ข้อ 14</small>	PathogenDx::Bacteria::gpr MED23-14
Two hours after eating <b>reheated fried rice</b> from a buffet that had been left at room temperature, a family of four develops sudden nausea, <b>vomiting</b>, and abdominal cramps with some diarrhea; vital signs are normal, and symptoms resolve <b>within 24 hours</b>. The illness is caused by a <b>preformed heat-stable emetic toxin</b> from a <b>spore-forming aerobic Gram-positive rod</b> whose spores survive cooking.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b><i>Bacillus cereus</i> (emetic type)</b><div><small>Aerobic Gram+ rod · spore-former · <b>cereulide</b> (heat-stable)</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Bacillus cereus food poisoning</b> (emetic type)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td><b>Vomiting 1–6 hrs</b> after the meal, cramps, ± diarrhea; resolves within 24 hrs</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td><b>Reheated fried rice</b> — spores survive cooking → preformed toxin</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td>Rice dishes kept at room temperature; eye trauma with foreign body (keratitis)</td></tr></table><ul><li><b>Diarrheal type</b>: diarrhea & abdominal pain <b>8–16 hrs</b></li><li><b>Heat-stable</b> toxin, <b>spore-former</b></li><li><b>Severe keratitis / endophthalmitis</b> หลัง trauma (foreign body); endocarditis, osteomyelitis ใน IVDU / medical devices</li></ul><small>Bacterial disease 69 · หน้า 22 · ★ โจทย์เก่า MED24 ข้อ 13</small>	PathogenDx::Bacteria::gpr MED24-13
A 40-year-old <b>goat and sheep butcher</b> notices a <b>painless papule</b> on his forearm 3 days after handling the <b>hide of a dead animal</b>; it becomes a vesicle and then an <b>ulcer covered by a black eschar</b>, with marked surrounding edema and regional lymphadenopathy. A 48-year-old <b>wool-sorting worker</b> develops a flu-like illness with fever, malaise, and dry cough, followed 3 days later by abrupt severe dyspnea, chest pain, and shock. Chest radiograph shows a <b>widened mediastinum</b> from <b>hemorrhagic mediastinitis</b>, and he dies within 24 hours. A 72-year-old man on immunosuppressive therapy develops fever, headache, neck stiffness, and confusion after eating <b>unpasteurized soft cheese</b> and deli meats. CSF Gram stain shows <b>Gram-positive rods</b>; the organism shows <b>tumbling motility</b>, grows at <b>refrigerator temperature (4 °C)</b>, and is β-hemolytic. It causes about 10% of community-acquired meningitis, also affects <b>neonates</b>, and infection during <b>pregnancy</b> can cause stillbirth.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b><i>Listeria monocytogenes</i></b><div><small>Gram+ rod · <b>tumbling motility</b> · grows at 4 °C · facultative intracellular</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Listeriosis</b>: neonatal & elderly <b>meningitis</b>, sepsis</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>Fever, headache, neck stiffness; pregnancy: flu-like illness → abortion / stillbirth</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td>Meningeal signs; neonate: granulomatosis infantiseptica</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td><b>Unpasteurized milk, soft cheese</b>, deli meats · transplacental / birth canal</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td><b>Neonates, pregnant women, elderly, immunocompromised</b></td></tr></table><ul><li>Neonates (&lt;1 month): <b>GBS</b> + <i>Listeria</i></li><li>Elderly / immunocompromised: <i>Listeria</i></li></ul><small>Bacterial disease 69 · หน้า 29–30</small>	PathogenDx::Bacteria::gpr
An <b>unimmunized</b> 6-year-old girl has fever, sore throat, <b>hoarseness</b>, and <b>inspiratory stridor</b>. Massive <b>cervical lymphadenopathy</b> with soft-tissue swelling gives a <b>“bull-neck” appearance</b>. A thick, <b>adherent, dirty-grey pseudomembrane</b> covers the tonsils and posterior pharynx and <b>bleeds when dislodged</b>. A 3-month-old unimmunized infant has 1 week of mild cough, sneezing, and rhinorrhea (<b>catarrhal stage</b>), followed by <b>paroxysms of explosive coughing</b> that end in an <b>inspiratory “whoop”</b>, <b>post-tussive vomiting</b>, cyanosis, and apnea (<b>paroxysmal stage</b>). This organism also belongs to the culture-negative endocarditis group.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b><i>Eikenella corrodens</i></b><div><small>Gram− bacillus · HACEK</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Human bite infection</b> · clenched-fist injury · HACEK endocarditis</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>Pain, swelling, purulent discharge at a bite / knuckle wound</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td>Cellulitis / septic arthritis of the <b>MCP joint</b> (fist fight)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td><b>Human bite</b> (human oral flora) — mixed with anaerobes, strep, staph</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td>Hands (clenched-fist injury)</td></tr></table><ul><li>เป็นหนึ่งใน <b>HACEK</b> → infective endocarditis ได้</li></ul><small>Bacterial disease 69 · หน้า 45, 49</small>	PathogenDx::Bacteria::zoo
A 12-year-old boy from North Carolina develops fever, severe headache, and myalgia a week after a camping trip during which he removed a <b>tick</b> from his scalp. On day 3, a maculopapular rash starts on the <b>wrists and ankles</b>, spreads to the <b>palms and soles</b>, and then moves <b>centrally to the trunk</b>, becoming petechial. The obligate intracellular organism infects endothelial cells, causing <b>necrotizing vasculitis</b>, and is treated with <b>doxycycline</b>.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b><i>Rickettsia rickettsii</i></b><div><small>Obligate intracellular Gram− · spotted fever group · necrotizing vasculitis</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Rocky Mountain spotted fever</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>Fever, headache, myalgia → rash (day 2–5) → sepsis</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td>Rash starts at <b>wrists & ankles</b> → <b>palms & soles</b> → spreads <b>centrally</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td><b>Tick</b> bite</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td>Americas (south-eastern US)</td></tr></table><ul><li>Rickettsiae destroy <b>arterioles & capillaries</b> → <b>necrotizing vasculitis</b></li><li>Spotted fever & scrub typhus groups: <b>eschar</b> · typhus group: <b>no eschar</b></li><li>Rx: <b>doxycycline</b></li></ul><small>Bacterial disease 69 · หน้า 65–66</small>	PathogenDx::Bacteria::zoo
A 30-year-old woman living in an apartment building with a <b>house mouse infestation</b> develops a <b>painless papule that turns into a black eschar</b> at the site of a <b>mite bite</b>. A few days later she has fever, headache, and a generalized <b>papulovesicular rash resembling chickenpox</b>. In an overcrowded <b>refugee camp</b> in winter, with poor hygiene and <b>body lice infestation</b>, many people develop sudden high fever, severe headache, and a maculopapular rash that <b>starts on the trunk and spreads outward</b>, sparing the face, palms, and soles; <b>no eschar</b> is found. Infection occurs when <b>louse feces</b> are scratched into the skin. Decades later, a survivor has a milder <b>recrudescence</b> of the same illness.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b><i>Rickettsia prowazekii</i></b><div><small>Typhus group Rickettsia</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Epidemic typhus</b> · <b>Brill-Zinsser disease</b> (recrudescence)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>High fever, severe headache, rash</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td>Rash starts on the <b>trunk → spreads outward</b>, spares palms & soles; <b>no eschar</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td><b>Body louse feces</b> (<i>Pediculus humanus</i>) rubbed into the bite</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td>War, refugee camps, crowding, poor hygiene</td></tr></table><ul><li>Typhus group: <b>no eschar</b></li></ul><small>Bacterial disease 69 · หน้า 66</small>	PathogenDx::Bacteria::zoo
A 40-year-old market worker in an <b>urban port area infested with rats</b> develops fever, headache, myalgia, and a faint <b>truncal maculopapular rash</b>; <b>no eschar</b> is found. A 32-year-old <b>forest ranger</b> returns from a 10-day <b>trek through rural scrub jungle</b> in Thailand with high fever, <b>severe headache</b>, myalgia, generalized lymphadenopathy, and a diffuse <b>maculopapular rash on the trunk</b>. A 6-year-old girl whose grandfather has a <b>chronic cough with cavitary lung disease</b> has a positive interferon-γ release assay but no symptoms. Chest radiograph shows a small <b>subpleural nodule in the lower part of the upper lobe</b> with enlarged <b>hilar lymph nodes</b>; biopsy would show <b>caseating granulomas</b> (<b>Ghon complex</b>). In about 90% of children this primary infection heals as a calcified scar. It spreads by <b>airborne droplet nuclei</b>.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b><i>Mycobacterium tuberculosis</i></b><div><small>Acid-fast bacilli · M. tuberculosis complex · caseating granuloma</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Primary pulmonary tuberculosis</b> (Ghon complex)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>Usually <b>asymptomatic</b>; fatigue, weight loss, fever</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td><b>Ghon focus</b> (lower upper lobe / upper lower lobe) + <b>hilar LN</b> = Ghon complex</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td><b>Airborne droplet nuclei</b> from patients with active TB</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td>First exposure, children; miliary spread in immunocompromised</td></tr></table><ul><li><i>M. tuberculosis</i> complex: <i>M. tuberculosis</i>, <i>M. bovis</i>, <i>M. africanum</i>, <i>M. microti</i></li><li>Clinical: fatigue, weight loss, fever; most → <b>healed scar</b></li><li><b>Miliary TB</b>: lymphatic / hematogenous spread (liver, spleen, pancreas) โดยเฉพาะ immunocompromised</li></ul><small>Bacterial disease 69 · หน้า 54–57</small>	PathogenDx::Bacteria::myco

A 40-year-old man with AIDS develops headache, confusion, personality change, and left hemiparesis that progress over <b>several weeks</b>; he has had chronic <b>nodular skin ulcers</b>. Brain imaging shows <b>multiple space-occupying lesions</b>, and biopsy shows <b>granulomatous encephalitis</b> with trophozoites and double-walled cysts. The free-living organism lives in <b>soil and water</b> and reached the brain by <b>hematogenous spread</b> from the skin or lower respiratory tract.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b><i>Acanthamoeba</i> spp.</b><div><small>Free-living ameba</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Granulomatous amebic encephalitis</b> (GAE)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>Subacute headache, confusion, focal deficits, seizures over weeks–months</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td>Brain <b>mass lesion(s)</b>; skin ulcers / nodules may precede</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td><b>Hematogenous spread</b> from lower respiratory tract, skin or ulcer</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td><b>Water & soil</b> · <b>immunocompromised</b> hosts (AIDS, transplant)</td></tr></table><ul><li>พบใน <b>water & soil</b>; infects skin, lung, adrenals</li></ul><small>Parasitic infection · หน้า 2</small>	PathogenDx::Parasite::cns
A 25-year-old <b>soft contact lens wearer</b> who <b>rinses and stores her lenses in tap water</b> has 3 weeks of <b>severe eye pain out of proportion</b> to the findings, photophobia, and a <b>foreign-body sensation</b> that do not respond to antibacterial drops. A newborn has <b>hydrocephalus</b>, <b>chorioretinitis</b>, and diffuse <b>intracranial calcifications</b> on CT (the <b>classic triad</b>). His mother had no symptoms in pregnancy, but she cleaned the family <b>cat’s litter box</b>, and her older children play in a <b>sandbox</b> used by cats. A 35-year-old man with AIDS (CD4 count 60/µL) who is not taking prophylaxis has 2 weeks of headache, fever, confusion, and new right hemiparesis with a focal seizure. MRI shows <b>multiple ring-enhancing lesions</b> with <b>surrounding edema and mass effect</b> in the basal ganglia. A 28-year-old previously healthy woman has 2 weeks of fatigue, low-grade fever, headache, and painless <b>posterior cervical lymphadenopathy</b> (a <b>mononucleosis-like illness</b>), but the heterophile test is negative. Four patients with meningitis have these CSF findings: (A) <b>eosinophil predominance</b>, raised protein, <b>normal glucose</b>; (B) WBC <b>≥1,000/µL, mostly neutrophils</b>, glucose <b>≤40 mg/dL</b>; (C) WBC <b>&lt;100/µL, mostly lymphocytes</b>, <b>normal glucose</b>, normal opening pressure; (D) <b>lymphocytes</b>, raised protein, and <b>low glucose (&lt;45 mg/dL)</b>.<br><br><b>Which category of pathogen best fits each CSF profile?</b>	<b>Parasite · Bacterial · Viral · TB/Fungal</b><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td>Typical CSF findings in meningitis</td></tr></table><ul><li>Parasite: ↑OP, variable WBC, <b>eosinophils</b>, ↑protein, <b>normal glucose</b></li><li>Bacterial: ↑OP, WBC ≥1,000/µL, <b>neutrophils</b>, mild–marked ↑protein, glucose ≤40 mg/dL</li><li>Viral: OP usually normal, WBC &lt;100/µL, <b>lymphocytes</b> (PMN early), normal glucose</li><li>Fungal / TB: <b>lymphocytes</b>, ↑protein, <b>↓glucose</b> (TB อาจ &lt;45 mg/dL)</li><li><b>PAM</b> (<i>Naegleria</i>): CSF profile เหมือน bacterial</li></ul><small>Parasitic infection · หน้า 7</small>	PathogenDx::Parasite::cns
A 9-year-old boy from a rural <b>mud-walled house in Bolivia</b> develops high fever, malaise, and painless <b>swelling of one eyelid with conjunctivitis (Romaña sign)</b> after being bitten near the eye at night; he also has a painful indurated red nodule on the cheek. A 35-year-old aid worker returns from rural <b>West Africa</b> with a painful indurated nodule at the site of a <b>tsetse fly bite</b>, followed by <b>intermittent fever</b>, headache, myalgia, and <b>enlarged posterior cervical lymph nodes</b> (<b>Winterbottom’s sign</b>). A 25-year-old soldier returns from a jungle patrol on the <b>Thai–Myanmar border</b> with <b>abrupt high fever (41 °C) and shaking chills</b>, headache, vomiting, and myalgia about <b>2 weeks after mosquito bites</b>. Two days later he becomes confused and has a seizure (<b>cerebral malaria</b>), passes <b>dark cola-colored urine</b> (<b>blackwater fever</b>), and is jaundiced and anemic with splenomegaly. Thin smear shows <b>multiple small ring forms per RBC</b>, high parasitemia, and <b>banana-shaped gametocytes</b>.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b><i>Plasmodium falciparum</i></b><div><small>Apicomplexa · multiple ring forms, banana-shaped gametocytes</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Severe (falciparum) malaria</b>: cerebral malaria, blackwater fever</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>Abrupt fever & chills (up to 41 °C), headache, N/V → <b>altered consciousness, seizures</b>, dark urine, dyspnea</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td>Continuous / irregular fever; <b>anemia, splenomegaly</b>, jaundice; capillary blockage</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td>Female <b>Anopheles</b> mosquito (ยุงก้นปล่อง) · blood transfusion</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td><b>Forested border areas</b> of Thailand (Thai–Myanmar, Thai–Cambodia), sub-Saharan Africa · RBCs</td></tr></table><ul><li><b>Capillary blockage</b> → potentially life-threatening if untreated</li><li>Tertian แต่ fever อาจ continuous / briefly remittent</li><li>Dx: <b>thick and thin Giemsa-stained smears</b> ทุก 6–12 ชม. จนครบ 48 ชม., serology, PCR</li></ul><small>Parasitic infection · หน้า 16–17</small>	PathogenDx::Parasite::blood
A 30-year-old forest worker from the Thai–Myanmar border has paroxysms of chills, high fever, and <b>drenching sweats every 48 hours</b> (<b>tertian</b>) and feels well between attacks. He has <b>another attack 8 months after</b> treatment with chloroquine alone, without re-exposure. Thin smear shows ameboid trophozoites in <b>enlarged RBCs with Schüffner dots</b>. The relapse comes from dormant <b>hypnozoites in the liver</b>, so <b>primaquine</b> is needed.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b><i>Plasmodium vivax</i> / <i>P. ovale</i></b><div><small>Apicomplexa · <b>hypnozoites</b> in liver · enlarged RBCs with Schüffner dots</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Relapsing tertian malaria</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>Paroxysms every 48 hrs: chills → high fever → drenching sweats; well between attacks</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td>Splenomegaly, anemia; <b>relapse months–years later</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td>Female <b>Anopheles</b> mosquito</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td>P. vivax: most common malaria in <b>Thailand</b> & Asia · P. ovale: Africa · dormant in <b>liver</b></td></tr></table><ul><li>Non-falciparum malaria: usually <b>self-limited</b>, low mortality</li><li>ต้องให้ยาที่ kill hypnozoites (เช่น <b>primaquine</b>) เพื่อป้องกัน relapse</li></ul><small>Parasitic infection · หน้า 16–17</small>	PathogenDx::Parasite::blood ไฮไลต์ในชีท
A 40-year-old woman from West Africa has recurring fever with chills <b>every 72 hours</b> (<b>quartan</b>)—Monday, then Thursday, then Sunday—and feels fairly well in between, but she later develops <b>nephrotic syndrome</b>. Thin smear shows <b>band-form trophozoites</b> and <b>rosette schizonts</b> in normal-sized RBCs.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b><i>Plasmodium malariae</i></b><div><small>Apicomplexa · band forms, rosette schizonts</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Quartan malaria</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>Fever every <b>72 hrs</b> (every 3rd day), milder course</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td>Chronic infection → nephrotic syndrome</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td>Female <b>Anopheles</b> mosquito</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td>Tropics worldwide</td></tr></table><ul><li><b>Tertian</b> (every 48 hrs): <i>P. vivax</i>, <i>P. ovale</i>, <i>P. falciparum</i></li></ul><small>Parasitic infection · หน้า 16</small>	PathogenDx::Parasite::blood
A 70-year-old man from <b>Massachusetts, USA</b>, who had a <b>splenectomy</b>, develops fever, fatigue, dark urine, and jaundice 2 weeks after hiking in woods where <b>deer ticks (Ixodes scapularis)</b> are common. Labs show <b>hemolytic anemia</b> and <b>thrombocytopenia</b>. A Giemsa-stained blood film shows intraerythrocytic ring forms and <b>tetrads of merozoites (Maltese cross)</b> with <b>no brown pigment</b>. The reservoir is the <b>white-footed mouse</b>.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b><i>Babesia microti</i></b><div><small>Apicomplexa · intraerythrocytic rings, <b>tetrad (Maltese cross)</b>, no pigment</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Babesiosis</b> (malaria-like illness)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>Fever, fatigue, dark urine; severe in splenectomy / elderly</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td><b>Hemolytic anemia</b>, thrombocytopenia, jaundice</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td><b>Ixodes scapularis</b> (deer tick, nymph) bite · transfusion · transplacental (rare)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td><b>United States</b> (Northeast), Europe · reservoir: <b>white-footed mice</b></td></tr></table><ul><li>Dx: <b>Giemsa blood film</b>, serology (IFA), PCR</li></ul><small>Parasitic infection · หน้า 17</small>	PathogenDx::Parasite::blood
A 45-year-old man from a village on the <b>Thai–Myanmar border</b> has had recurrent fever with painful lymphangitis for years and now has massive swelling of the <b>whole leg extending above the knee</b> (<b>elephantiasis</b>) and a hydrocele. A <b>thick blood smear taken at night</b> shows sheathed <b>microfilariae</b>. Local vectors include <b>Aedes niveus</b>, <b>Mansonia dives</b>, and <b>Culex quinquefasciatus</b>, and the adult worms live in the <b>lymphatics</b>.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b><i>Wuchereria bancrofti</i></b><div><small>Filarial nematode · sheathed microfilaria, nocturnal periodicity</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Lymphatic filariasis</b> (bancroftian) — elephantiasis</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>Recurrent fever + lymphangitis → chronic limb swelling</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td><b>Elephantiasis above the knee</b> (whole leg); hydrocele</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td><b>Aedes niveus group</b> (ยุงลายป่า), <b>Mansonia dives</b> (ยุงลายเสือ), <b>Culex quinquefasciatus</b> (ยุงรำคาญ)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td><b>Thai–Myanmar border</b> · adult worms in <b>lymph nodes / lymphatics</b></td></tr></table><ul><li>Adult worms ใน <b>lymph nodes</b> → inflammation → <b>lymphatic obstruction</b></li><li>Tx: <b>diethylcarbamazine (DEC)</b> (microfilariae only)</li></ul><small>Parasitic infection · หน้า 18</small>	PathogenDx::Parasite::blood ไฮไลต์ในชีท
A 40-year-old rubber tapper from a swampy area of <b>southern Thailand (Narathiwat)</b> has recurrent fever and lymphadenitis followed by chronic swelling of the <b>leg below the knee</b> (<b>elephantiasis</b>). A <b>night-time thick blood smear</b> shows sheathed <b>microfilariae</b>. A 6-year-old girl from a rural village who plays in <b>soil contaminated with human feces</b> has colicky abdominal pain, distension, and vomiting; an abdominal radiograph shows a bolus of worms causing <b>small-bowel obstruction</b>, and she vomits a 20-cm <b>pink roundworm</b>. An 8-year-old boy in <b>rural southern Thailand</b> who <b>walks barefoot</b> on moist soil has progressive pallor, lethargy, epigastric discomfort, and pica, and recalls an <b>itchy rash on his feet (ground itch)</b> months ago. Infection began when <b>filariform larvae penetrated the skin</b>.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b>Hookworm (<i>Necator americanus</i> / <i>Ancylostoma duodenale</i>)</b><div><small>Intestinal nematode (small bowel) · thin-shelled oval egg · filariform larva</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Hookworm infection</b> (พยาธิปากขอ) → <b>iron-deficiency anemia</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td><b>Pallor</b>, fatigue, epigastric discomfort; itchy rash at entry site (<b>ground itch</b>)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td><b>Microcytic hypochromic anemia</b>, eosinophilia; Löffler’s syndrome</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td><b>Filariform larvae penetrate skin</b> — walking barefoot on soil</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td><b>Rural moist soil</b> (Southern Thailand), farmers · adults suck blood in <b>small intestine</b></td></tr></table><ul><li><b>Percutaneous penetration of filariform larvae</b> → lung (Löffler) → swallowed → <b>small intestine (blood sucking)</b></li><li><b>Larva migrans (ground itch)</b></li></ul><small>Parasitic infection · หน้า 19–20, 22 · ★ โจทย์เก่า MED23 ข้อ 19</small>	PathogenDx::Parasite::nema MED23-19

A 28-year-old pig farmer from a rural area with poor sanitation has his <b>first generalized seizure</b> and chronic headaches. Brain CT shows multiple small <b>cysts each containing an eccentric dot (scolex)</b> and several <b>calcified cysts</b>, and he has painless subcutaneous nodules. He often eats <b>undercooked pork</b>, and a household member passes tapeworm segments. A 35-year-old man from <b>northeastern Thailand</b> who often eats <b>raw beef larb (laab neua)</b> notices <b>motile white flat segments crawling out of his anus</b> and in his stool, with mild abdominal discomfort and nausea. A 5-year-old child in an <b>orphanage</b> has mild abdominal pain, diarrhea, and poor appetite, and several other children are infected. Stool shows small, thin-shelled eggs with a hooked embryo and <b>polar filaments</b>. This <b>dwarf tapeworm</b>, the most common tapeworm in the US, needs <b>no intermediate host</b> because its eggs are <b>directly infectious</b> and allow <b>autoinfection</b>, though it can also be acquired by swallowing infected <b>fleas or grain beetles</b>.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b><i>Hymenolepis nana</i></b><div><small>Cestode · egg with <b>polar filaments</b> · intermediate host not required</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Hymenolepiasis</b> (dwarf tapeworm)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>Mostly asymptomatic; abdominal pain, diarrhea, anorexia</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td>Ingest <b>eggs</b> directly (fecal-oral, <b>autoinfection</b>) or cysticercoids in <b>fleas, grain beetles</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td><b>Children</b>, institutions; most common tapeworm in the US · small intestine</td></tr></table><ul><li>Asymptomatic หรือ <b>GI distress</b></li><li>Dx: <b>eggs in stool</b> — <i>H. diminuta</i> eggs <b>2× larger</b> and <b>lack polar filaments</b></li></ul><small>Parasitic infection · หน้า 25</small>	PathogenDx::Parasite::cest ไฮไลต์ในชีท

One week after an outdoor <b>wedding banquet</b> that served <b>fresh raspberries and basil</b>, 30 guests develop prolonged <b>watery diarrhea</b>, abdominal cramps, fatigue, anorexia, and low-grade fever. A <b>modified acid-fast stain</b> of stool shows <b>round oocysts 8–10 µm</b> with <b>variable acid-fast staining</b> that <b>autofluoresce under UV light</b>. Person-to-person spread is unlikely because the oocysts must <b>sporulate outside the host</b>.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b><i>Cyclospora cayetanensis</i></b><div><small>Apicomplexa · oocyst <b>8–10 µm</b>, variable acid-fast, <b>autofluorescent</b></small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Cyclosporiasis</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>Prolonged <b>watery diarrhea</b>, cramps, fatigue, low-grade fever, weight loss</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td><b>Contaminated fresh produce</b> (berries, lettuce, herbs) & water — oocysts must sporulate outside the host</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td>Food-borne outbreaks (banquets), travelers to tropics · small intestine</td></tr></table><ul><li>Oocyst size: <i>Cryptosporidium</i> 4–5 µm &lt; <b><i>Cyclospora</i> 8–10 µm</b> &lt; <i>Cystoisospora</i> 20–30 µm</li><li>Non-bloody diarrhea, <b>malabsorption</b>, weight loss, fatty stool; severe ใน immunocompromised / infants</li></ul><small>Parasitic infection · หน้า 32–33 · ★ โจทย์เก่า MED23 ข้อ 17</small>	PathogenDx::Parasite::proto MED23-17
A 40-year-old man with AIDS has chronic <b>non-bloody watery diarrhea</b>, fatty stools, <b>malabsorption</b>, and weight loss. His blood count shows <b>peripheral eosinophilia</b>, which is unusual for a protozoan infection. A <b>modified acid-fast stain</b> of stool shows <b>large oval oocysts 20–30 µm</b> containing sporoblasts, and the oocyst wall <b>autofluoresces under UV light</b>. He acquired it from contaminated food or water.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b><i>Cystoisospora</i> (<i>Isospora</i>) <i>belli</i></b><div><small>Apicomplexa · large oval oocyst <b>20–30 µm</b>, acid-fast</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Cystoisosporiasis</b> (isosporiasis)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>Chronic <b>non-bloody watery diarrhea</b>, fatty stool, malabsorption, weight loss</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td><b>Eosinophilia</b> (unusual for protozoa)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td>Contaminated food / water (oocysts sporulate outside the host)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td><b>AIDS</b> / immunocompromised, tropics · small intestine</td></tr></table><ul><li>Oocyst wall <b>autofluoresces</b> under UV</li></ul><small>Parasitic infection · หน้า 32</small>	PathogenDx::Parasite::proto
Weeks after a holiday on a <b>Malaysian island</b>, 30 tourists develop fever, <b>severe myalgia</b>, and muscle tenderness (<b>myositis</b>); muscle biopsy shows elongated <b>intramuscular cysts filled with bradyzoites</b> and eosinophilic myositis. Other travelers who ate <b>undercooked beef or pork</b> in Southeast Asia have only <b>self-limited diarrhea</b>, and their stools contain autofluorescent <b>sporocysts</b>.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b><i>Sarcocystis</i> spp.</b><div><small>Apicomplexa · sporocysts in stool · sarcocysts in muscle</small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Sarcocystosis</b> — intestinal / muscular</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>Intestinal: self-limited diarrhea, mild fever, N/V · muscular: <b>myositis, myalgia</b>, fever</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td>Muscle biopsy: <b>sarcocysts</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td>Undercooked <b>beef (S. hominis)</b> / <b>pork (S. suihominis)</b>; muscular form: sporocysts from other animals</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td><b>Southeast Asia, Malaysia</b></td></tr></table><ul><li><i>S. hominis</i> (cattle), <i>S. suihominis</i> (pig) → intestinal sarcocystosis</li><li>Stool: <b>oocysts 15–20 µm with 2 sporocysts</b> / sporocysts (autofluorescence)</li></ul><small>Parasitic infection · หน้า 33–34</small>	PathogenDx::Parasite::proto
A 58-year-old man from <b>Khon Kaen, northeastern Thailand</b>, who has eaten <b>koi pla (raw fish salad)</b> and <b>pla ra (fermented fish)</b> made from <b>freshwater cyprinoid fish</b> since childhood, has dyspepsia, right upper quadrant pain, weight loss, and progressive <b>painless jaundice</b>. Imaging shows dilated intrahepatic bile ducts and a hilar mass (<b>cholangiocarcinoma</b>). Stool shows <b>small operculated eggs with opercular shoulders and an abopercular knob</b>; the adult flukes live in the <b>bile ducts</b>.<br><br><b>What is the most likely causative pathogen?</b>	<b><i>Opisthorchis viverrini</i></b><div><small>Trematode · small egg with <b>opercular shoulder + abopercular knob</b></small></div><table><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">โรค</th><td><b>Opisthorchiasis</b> (liver fluke, พยาธิใบไม้ตับ) → <b>cholangiocarcinoma</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">อาการ</th><td>Mild: dyspepsia, abdominal pain, diarrhea / constipation → RUQ pain, jaundice</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">Sign</th><td>Hepatomegaly, cholangitis, cholecystitis; late: <b>cholangiocarcinoma</b></td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">พาหะ · การติดต่อ</th><td>Ingest <b>raw / salted freshwater (cyprinoid) fish</b> with metacercariae (ก้อยปลา, ปลาร้า, ปลาส้ม)</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:left;vertical-align:top;padding:2px 10px 2px 0;white-space:nowrap">ที่พบ</th><td><b>Northeast Thailand</b> (อีสาน), Laos, Cambodia · adults in <b>bile ducts</b></td></tr></table><ul><li><b>Metacercariae</b> ใน fish muscle / under the scales</li><li>Egg: <b>opercular shoulder + abopercular knob</b></li><li>CCA pathogenesis: chronic inflammation, <b>periductal fibrosis</b>, endogenous & exogenous <b>nitrosamines</b></li></ul><small>Parasitic infection · หน้า 35–36</small>	PathogenDx::Parasite::trem
A 45-year-old farmer from <b>northern Thailand</b> has fever, <b>right upper quadrant pain</b>, tender hepatomegaly, an urticarial rash, and progressive <b>jaundice</b> with raised direct bilirubin and ALP; his blood count shows marked <b>eosinophilia</b>. A 12-year-old boy from a pig-raising village in <b>central Thailand</b>, who often peels raw <b>water caltrop and water chestnuts</b> with his teeth, has abdominal pain, chronic diarrhea, facial edema, and later signs of <b>intestinal obstruction</b>. A 35-year-old man from northern Thailand who eats <b>raw snails, clams, and freshwater fish</b> has mild abdominal pain, diarrhea, and low-grade fever.
